title: A permissible blowup preserves the boundary and its strict exceptional part
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), let $B\subset X$ be a normal crossings divisor, and let $H\subset B$ be a reduced union of irreducible components which is a strict normal crossings divisor; $H=\varnothing$ is allowed. A normal crossings divisor means a reduced effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor) [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] which, etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism], has equation $t_1\cdots t_r=0$ for distinct members of a regular system of parameters; a regular system of parameters in a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is a set of $\dim R$ elements generating $\mathfrak m$. Here a strict normal crossings divisor has regular irreducible components, and every intersection of $s$ distinct components is empty or regular with every irreducible component of codimension $s$ in $X$. Let $M\subset B$ be a regular closed subscheme such that etale locally at each point of $M$, in parameters giving the above equation for $B$, its ideal is generated by a nonempty subset of those parameters. Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_M(X)\to X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], let $E=(b^{-1}M)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and put $B^+=(b^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $H^+=(b^{-1}(H\cup M))_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $X^+$ is regular, $B^+$ is a normal crossings divisor, and $H^+$ is a strict normal crossings divisor and a union of irreducible components of $B^+$. In particular $H^+$ has finitely many regular irreducible components and every intersection of $s$ distinct components is empty or regular of codimension $s$ in $X^+$. As reduced closed subschemes, $B^+=B^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$ and $H^+=H^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$, where the superscript denotes strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform].

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; the regular-intersection criterion is Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118.

proof.text: The center has finite-type ideal because $X$ is Noetherian. The blowup is proper by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X^+$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives finite component families for $H$ and for the closed subschemes of $X^+$. Away from $M$, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] gives $X^+\setminus E\simeq X\setminus M$. Under this isomorphism [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-restrict] identifies each strict transform with its original boundary restricted to $X\setminus M$, compatibly with projection. All the asserted regularity and boundary properties on this open are therefore inherited from $X,B,H$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 4.1.2 and Remark 4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 hypotheses, printed p. 121

proof.text: Fix $y\in E$ and $x=b(y)$. Choose an actual étale neighborhood $v:W\to X$, a point $w$ over $x$, and parameters in $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$ such that $B$ has equation $t_1\cdots t_r=0$ and $M$ has ideal $(t_j:j\in J)$. Here $J\ne\varnothing$ and $J\cap\{1,\ldots,r\}\ne\varnothing$ since $M\subset B$. Choose representatives on an affine open $W^\circ$ around $w$ retaining these equations. As $H$ is a reduced union of components of $B$, its pullback is the union of a subset of these coordinate hyperplanes, with equation $\prod_{i\in I}t_i=0$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-component-coordinate-identification] on $X$ with $D=H$ and with $H_a$ the actual distinct irreducible components of $H$, which are regular by hypothesis. After shrinking $W^\circ$, each $H_a$ through $x$ pulls back to one distinct hyperplane $V(t_{i(a)})$ and the others miss $w$; the same statement supplies the generic-point hypothesis for strict-transform base change. This application concerns only the original components on $X$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118

proof.text: Form $Y=X^+\times_XW^\circ$. The projection $Y\to X^+$ is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] identifies $Y$ with the blowup of $W^\circ$ in the pulled-back center. Choose $\tilde y$ in the fiber over the pair $(y,w)$, that is a point of $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(y)\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(w))$; this tensor product of two field extensions is nonzero. Choose a standard chart through $\tilde y$. Its local ring at $\tilde y$ is a localization of the chart ring over $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$. By [lem-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart] this ring is regular, the reduced pullback of $B$ is a union of coordinate hyperplanes, and all coordinate intersections have the stated regularity and codimension. For each $H_a$, first use its hyperplane identification at $w$ from step 2, then [lem-trf-strict-transform-flat-etale-base-change] to identify $(H_a^{\mathrm{st}})\times_XW^\circ$ with the strict transform of that hyperplane, and finally the strict-transform clause of [lem-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart]. It follows that near $\tilde y$ this pullback is empty or one strict-transform coordinate hyperplane, distinct for distinct $a$. The reduced exceptional inverse image is the additional coordinate hyperplane $t_j=0$. No regularity of $H_a^{\mathrm{st}}$ has been assumed.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118

proof.text: The étale neighborhoods from step 3 and $X^+\setminus E$ cover $X^+$. By [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent], pullback of each reduced inverse image is the reduced subscheme on its pulled-back support; hence the calculated coordinate products are the actual pullbacks of $B^+$ and $H^+$, and their effective Cartier property descends. These equations directly make $B^+$ normal crossings. Consider the finite family consisting of $E$ and all nonempty $H_a^{\mathrm{st}}$. At every étale point in step 3 its members are empty or distinct coordinate hyperplanes, so every selected intersection is empty or regular of the expected codimension. Off $E$ the same holds by the original SNC hypothesis and step 1. Apply [lem-trf-etale-regular-intersection-descent] to this family, including the empty intersection $X^+$, to obtain regularity of the ambient scheme, of each member, and of every intersection, with the asserted codimensions. In particular $E$ is regular and Noetherian; [rem-pc-regular-normal] says that its irreducible components are disjoint open and closed subschemes. They inherit the regular local rings of $E$. Each nonempty $H_a^{\mathrm{st}}$ is irreducible, being the closure of the irreducible open $H_a\setminus M$ under the isomorphism of step 1. Thus passing from $E$ to its disjoint components preserves the intersection conclusions. This proves that the actual irreducible components of $H^+$ and all their intersections satisfy the SNC criterion; no component-identification lemma is applied to $H^+$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118

proof.text: On the complement of $E$ the strict transforms agree with the original divisors by step 1. On every chart of step 3 the reduced inverse images are exactly the union of the surviving strict-transform hyperplanes and the exceptional hyperplane. The closure definition [def-nagata-strict-transform] and reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] consequently give the reduced closed-subscheme equalities $B^+=B^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$ and $H^+=H^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$. Each hyperplane of $H^+$ occurs among those of $B^+$, so each irreducible component of $H^+$ is an irreducible component of $B^+$. Finiteness follows from step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]; regularity and all intersection codimensions follow from step 4. The empty product $\prod_{i\in\varnothing}t_i=1$ includes $H=\varnothing$, when $H^+=E$.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned false component-identification statement by requiring exactly the distinct irreducible components and defining coordinates by a regular system of parameters. Removed its strict-transform proof sketch. The proof now identifies the original H components on X, base-changes their strict transforms, and then applies the blowup chart clause at a point over both y and w, without assuming regularity of the transforms. Added strict-transform restriction off the center, corrected the flat base-change source to Stacks 081I and the flatness definition dependency, and removed the worker-written tool_uses.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes ILO VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), Remark 4.2.2(i), and Lemma 4.2.9 coordinate-chart proof; the new base-change/component statements make the étale-local strict-transform argument explicit.

The item's statement is unchanged. It assumes M in B, which is stronger than ILO's 'V has normal crossings with Z'; that is fine because the item is not a target and its only user, the strictification step, blows up centers inside the boundary. It holds on A^2 axes/origin, a Cartier center, a nodal B, A^3 with M=V(x,z), and H empty. Steps 1-5 check out: J meets {1..r} because (t_J) is prime and contains t_1...t_r. The component lemma is applied only to H on X, and its hypotheses hold. A point over (y,w) exists because the residue-field tensor product is nonzero. Strict-transform flat base change follows from 081I. The descent lemma is applied to the family {E, H_a^st}, then rem-pc-regular-normal passes the result to the components of E. The set equalities for B^+ and H^+ are immediate. All 4 new nodes are true, statement-only and self-contained, with correct blueprint.from/via. No duplicates found by rg over strict transform, 081I/080F, SNC, permissible, RSP and 025N/039S. The strict-transform node's generic-point hypothesis is stronger than needed but harmless, and step 2 supplies it. FIX: the corrected lem-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart.json restores '\ne', which had become a literal newline followed by 'e' (B4). It also makes the strict-transform clause explicit: on chart j the strict transform of V(t_i) is V(u_i) for i in J\{j}, empty for i=j and V(t_i) for i not in J. Step 3 uses exactly this identification. Accepted tool uses: thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper, thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement, lemma-nagata-strict-transform-restrict, thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change, rem-pc-regular-normal. lean.statement: theorem permissible_boundary_preservation (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (hX : IsRegularScheme X) (B H M : X.IdealSheafData) (hB : B.IsNormalCrossingsDivisor) (hH : IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary H) (hHB : (H.support : Set X) ⊆ (B.support : Set X)) (hHcomponents : IsUnionOfIrreducibleComponents H B) (hM : IsPermissibleCenter B M) : IsRegularScheme M.blowup ∧ ((B.comap M.blowupMap).radical).IsNormalCrossingsDivisor ∧ IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary ((H ⊓ M).comap M.blowupMap).radical ∧ (((H ⊓ M).comap M.blowupMap).radical.support : Set M.blowup) ⊆ (((B.comap M.blowupMap).radical).support : Set M.blowup) ∧ IsUnionOfIrreducibleComponents ((H ⊓ M).comap M.blowupMap).radical ((B.comap M.blowupMap).radical) ∧ (B.comap M.blowupMap).radical = strictTransformIdeal M B ⊓ (M.comap M.blowupMap).radical ∧ ((H ⊓ M).comap M.blowupMap).radical = strictTransformIdeal M H ⊓ (M.comap M.blowupMap).radical
